content.user_title: Build Azure Voice Live Python Apps
content.value_statement: Real-time voice AI apps need streaming audio, session setup, and Azure authentication. This skill guides Python developers through Voice Live connections, audio buffers, VAD, function calls, and event handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure AI Voice Live Python package and required dependencies.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and API key authentication patterns for Azure Cognitive Services.
Demonstrates session setup for text and audio modalities, voices, VAD, and function tools.
Covers sending and receiving base64 PCM16 audio through Voice Live buffers.
Lists key event types for transcripts, audio deltas, function calls, and errors.
Summarizes voice choices, audio formats, turn detection options, and interruption handling.
limitations: Requires an Azure Cognitive Services resource and valid credentials.
Provides guidance and snippets, not a complete production application.
Does not replace Azure service documentation for quotas, pricing, or regional availability.
Production security, privacy, and compliance controls must be designed separately.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Create a Python proof of concept that connects to Voice Live and streams microphone audio.

use_cases.title: Add Voice to Support Workflows
use_cases.description: Use audio events, transcription, and function calls to design voice-enabled support tools.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Voice Interaction Settings
use_cases.description: Compare voices, audio formats, and turn detection modes before building a user-facing app.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Quick Start
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal Python quick start for Azure AI Voice Live. Include installation, environment variables, DefaultAzureCredential, and a simple event loop.

prompt_templates.title: Add Audio Streaming
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me send microphone PCM16 audio to Azure AI Voice Live and play received audio. Explain buffer append, commit, and response events.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Conversation Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Voice Live session for a concise assistant. Configure voice, audio format, server VAD, transcription, and interruption handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Tool-Enabled Voice App
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an architecture for a production Python voice assistant using Voice Live function tools, error handling, authentication, and secure secret management.

output_examples.input: I need a quick start for a Python voice assistant with Azure AI Voice Live.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan with dependency installation, Azure endpoint setup, DefaultAzureCredential usage, session creation, and event handling steps.

output_examples.input: I want to support interruptions during spoken responses.
output_examples.output: Guidance to listen for speech started events, cancel the active response, clear the output buffer, and then accept the next user turn.

output_examples.input: I need to choose audio and turn detection settings for a prototype.
output_examples.output: A comparison of PCM16 formats, telephony formats, server VAD, semantic VAD, and practical selection guidance for common voice app scenarios.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential for production and keep API keys out of source control.
Validate audio sample rate, channel count, and format before streaming buffers.
Handle error, cancellation, interruption, and connection closed events explicitly.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding Azure keys or endpoints into application source files.
Using example snippets as production code without retries, logging, and privacy controls.
Ignoring turn detection settings when users may interrupt long spoken responses.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps build Python applications that use Azure AI Voice Live for real-time voice interaction.

faq.question: Does it provide a complete app?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused snippets and patterns for connection, audio streaming, events, and session setup.

faq.question: Which authentication method should I use?
faq.answer: Use DefaultAzureCredential when possible. API key examples are included for simpler development setups.

faq.question: Can it support speech-to-speech experiences?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers text and audio modalities, audio buffers, received audio deltas, and transcripts.

faq.question: Does it cover function calling?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how function tools can be defined and how function call outputs are returned.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review Azure identity setup, secret handling, privacy requirements, error handling, latency, and regional service availability.
